cis_matches.control_title: Disable password authentication in favor of key-based SSH login
cis_matches.text: SSH should be configured to disable password authentication and require public-key authentication instead, reducing exposure to credential-stuffing and brute-force attacks. Combine this with disabling root login over SSH and restricting access to specific source networks where feasible.

raw_output: VULNERABLE: ssh-agent PKCS#11 unsanitized search path enables remote code execution when agent is forwarded. IDs: CVE:CVE-2023-38408

cve_records.text: The PKCS#11 feature in ssh-agent in OpenSSH before 9.3p2 has an insufficiently trustworthy search path, leading to remote code execution if an agent is forwarded to an attacker-controlled system. (Code in /usr/lib is not necessarily safe for loading into ssh-agent.) NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2016-10009.

cis_matches.control_title: Keep web server software on a supported, patched version
cis_matches.text: Web server software should be kept current with vendor security patches, and end-of-life versions should be upgraded. Older Apache httpd releases have accumulated known vulnerabilities that are fixed in later maintenance branches; running an outdated version increases exposure without proportionate benefit.

cis_matches.control_title: Monitor and renew TLS certificates before expiry
cis_matches.text: TLS certificates should be tracked with automated expiry monitoring and renewed well before their expiration date. An expired certificate causes client trust warnings or hard connection failures, and in some client configurations, silently downgrades security expectations. Automated renewal (e.g. via ACME/Let's Encrypt or enterprise PKI tooling) is preferred over manual tracking.

raw_output: VULNERABLE: OpenSSL heartbeat extension buffer over-read leaks process memory (Heartbleed). Risk factor: HIGH  IDs: CVE:CVE-2014-0160

cve_records.text: The (1) TLS and (2) DTLS implementations in OpenSSL 1.0.1 before 1.0.1g do not properly handle Heartbeat Extension packets, which allows remote attackers to obtain sensitive information from process memory via crafted packets that trigger a buffer over-read, as demonstrated by reading private keys, related to d1_both.c and t1_lib.c, aka the Heartbleed bug.
